name: Galibi Carib

ancestors.notes: Descent per Glottolog classification of Galibi Carib (gali1262).

notes: Research. Cariban language (Kariña/Kali'na, a.k.a. Galibi Carib) of Venezuela and the Guianas, Latin orthography (Hoff 1968). The grapheme ï (also seen written ɨ in some sources/dictionaries, mapped equivalently) denotes the high central vowel /ɨ/. The glottal stop is written with an apostrophe, whose exact codepoint varies by source text (modifier letter apostrophe ʼ, right single quotation mark ’, or plain ASCII '); all three are mapped to /ʔ/. The voiced stops b/d/g overlap with post-nasal allophones of the voiceless stops p/t/k and are treated by some descriptions as conditioned rather than independent; they are mapped here at face value. Word stress falls on the final syllable in the disyllabic-dominant WOLD gold sample (Hoff 1968); marked here as final by default. Palatalization allophones ([tʃ ʃ ɲ]) and fricative allophones ([β]) that the spelling does not distinguish are left unencoded; there is no tone. The WOLD gold sample also contains a minority of French-loanword entries spelled in French orthography (e.g. ⟨fromage⟩, ⟨mercredi⟩) rather than adapted Kali'na spelling; these are outside this spec's Kali'na grapheme map and are not modelled.
